text: What happens when I donate blood?

args.label: Blood donation
args.source: Own estimate: a standard 470 ml whole-blood donation over about 10 minutes; heart rate rises a few beats and blood pressure dips slightly, plasma volume refills within 1-2 days (blood bank guidance, e.g. NHSBT/Red Cross).

feelings.label: Lightheaded
feelings.cause: Less blood volume, slightly lower blood pressure

feelings.label: Tired
feelings.cause: Fewer red cells carrying oxygen for weeks

stops.label: Arm vein
stops.say: About half a litre leaves through a needle in an arm vein over ten minutes.

stops.label: Heart
stops.say: Less blood returns, so the heart beats a little faster to keep pressure up.

stops.label: Kidneys
stops.say: Kidneys hold back water and make less urine to refill the plasma.

steps.title: Half a litre leaves
steps.say: As an example, you donate now. Over about ten minutes roughly half a litre, around a tenth of your blood, flows out through a needle in an arm vein.

composed.caption: Blood leaving an arm vein into the bag
composed.basis: Standard whole-blood donation, about 470 ml in 8 to 12 minutes (blood service guidance)

steps.title: The heart speeds up
steps.say: Less blood comes back to the heart, so each beat pushes out a little less. Pressure sensors notice and speed it up, from about 78 to 86 beats a minute.

steps.title: Vessels tighten, maybe lightheaded
steps.say: Your blood pressure dips a little, so vessels in the gut and skin narrow to keep the brain supplied. If you stand too fast, you may feel lightheaded.

steps.title: Kidneys hold on to water
steps.say: Hormones tell your kidneys to send more filtered water back into the blood and make less urine. That is why they hand you a drink afterwards.

steps.title: Plasma refills in days
steps.say: Fluid seeps from the tissues back into your vessels, so the liquid part of the blood is back within a day or two. Your red cells are now more diluted.

composed.caption: Tissue fluid moving back into the blood
composed.basis: Starling forces: lower pressure in capillaries draws fluid in; plasma volume restores in 24 to 48 h (physiology textbooks)

steps.title: New red cells take weeks
steps.say: Your kidneys sense less oxygen and release erythropoietin, telling bone marrow to make red cells. Replacing them, and the iron they carry, takes about four to eight weeks.

composed.caption: Kidney signal drives marrow to make red cells
composed.basis: EPO feedback loop; red cell recovery after donation about 4 to 8 weeks (Kiss et al. 2015, JAMA)

lines.text: In the model your heart rate rises from about 78 to 86 after giving half a litre.
Your kidneys hold on to water, so fluid returns within two days. Red cells take weeks.
Tonight's beer and leg day could make you feel more lightheaded, so donors skip both first.
